⏰ THE FILING DEADLINE IS NOT THE TIME TO HIRE YOUR ATTORNEY.
“My immigration hearing is still a month away. I have time to hire a lawyer.”
Your documents may already be due.
In many non-detained immigration court cases, supporting documents must be submitted at least 30 days before the individual hearing, unless the judge sets a different deadline. That is the deadline to file your materials—not to begin preparing them. 

Our recommendation: Hire your attorney at least 2–3 months before your individual hearing—and earlier whenever possible.
Your legal team needs time to review your case history, examine prior filings, gather supporting evidence, obtain translations, prepare declarations, research legal arguments, and organize your exhibits. Witness preparation and getting you ready to testify also require attention.
By the filing deadline, your attorney should be submitting carefully prepared materials—not opening your file for the first time.
Waiting until the last minute can leave too little time to prepare what your case needs. Late evidence may be excluded or given less weight, and late witness lists may prevent witnesses from testifying. 

📅 2–3 months before the hearing: Retain counsel and begin preparation.
📂 Before the filing deadline: Develop your evidence, declarations, and legal arguments.
⚖️ By the court’s deadline: Submit the required materials.
Give your legal team time to prepare—not just time to rush.

Y le hace su caso aún más fuerte si también había agresión, intimidación manipulación amenazas maltratos así pero muchas me preguntan qué evidencia necesita porque en la mayoría de los casos no hay tanta evidencia sobre lo que pasó y muchos tienen preocupación que no va a ganar porque no tiene pruebas. Pues aquí estoy con muy buenas noticias, las pruebas que necesita son su palabra Su palabra en este caso es suficiente en la mayoría de los casos Usted vas escribir una declaración Que sus historia escrita como muchos detalles sobre lo qué pasó y eso más qué suficiente para la mayoría de los casos. Y la razón que es suficiente su palabra es porque inmigración Es experto en estos casos, ¿verdad? Ello saben lo que pasa En Los trabajadores De Estados Unidos con Lo inmigrantes entonces ellos van a saber solo Su palabra si Si verdadero sí o no y hemos ganado mi firma montón estos casos con nada más que la palabra del aplicante. Entonces amigos, si usted sufrió maltratos especialmente maltratos sobre el pago en un trabajo aquí en los Estados Unidos no importa hace cuánto tiempo pasó esto vale la pena hablar con nosotros.
creatives.transcript_en: You all know it's possible to fix your papers because you were mistreated at work, right? But what evidence do you need about the mistreatment? I'm attorney Ángela Zinske, and if you worked in the past and didn't get fair pay, didn't get paid for all the hours you worked or all the jobs you did, many times it's possible to fix your papers because of this, even if it happened many years ago. And it makes your case even stronger if there was also aggression, intimidation, manipulation, threats, mistreatment like that. But a lot of people ask me what evidence they need, because in most cases there isn't much evidence of what happened, and many worry they won't win because they don't have proof. Well, I'm here with very good news: the proof you need is your word. Your word in this case is enough in most cases. You're going to write a statement, your story in writing with lots of details about what happened, and that's more than enough for most cases. And the reason your word is enough is because immigration is an expert in these cases, right? They know what happens to workers in the United States with immigrants, so they'll know from your word alone whether it's true or not, and my firm has won a ton of these cases with nothing more than the applicant's word. So, friends, if you were mistreated, especially mistreatment involving pay at a job here in the United States, no matter how long ago it happened, it's worth talking to us.

creatives.transcript_en: You don't need your child's help to fix your papers, and I'll tell you why. I'm attorney Ángeles Yensky, Immigration Attorney. Many people wonder how to fix based on having children if that child doesn't want to petition for them. Unfortunately, it's very common that for one reason or another your child DOESN'T WANT TO HELP YOU IN THE PROCESS OF FIXING YOUR PAPERS. It's a shame, but it's the reality. Thank God it's possible to fix on your own, without your child's help, based on having a citizen child who is going to turn 21. This case is called VAWA, and it's based not only on having a child but also on the problems you've had with this person. And if your relationship is at the point where your child doesn't want to petition for you, I imagine there are enough problems to qualify. So don't worry if you have a child who DOESN'T WANT TO PETITION FOR YOU. Call us! It doesn't matter if you have illegal entries, being caught, deportations, because despite all this it could be possible in many cases to fix on your own through your children without leaving

editorial_score.why: Hook names a common, painful situation: a citizen child who won't petition ('No necesita la ayuda de su hijo para arreglar').
editorial_score.check: Pathway is never named; 'no importa si tiene deportaciones... podría arreglar' is overbroad. Copy is election-timed ('después de elecciones'), so stale.

creatives.card_text_en: Call Us Today! | Were you told you can't fix your papers because of a permanent bar? ⚠️ You deserve a second opinion! There could still be ways to get papers through humanitarian cases like VAWA and the T Visa. Call us to learn your options! 📞 800-259-5555 | (800) 259-5555 | Call Now | Is it true that it's impossible to fix your papers if you have a permanent bar? I'm Attorney Angel Sinsky, an immigration attorney dedicated to getting papers for as many people as possible, especially people with difficult cases. Many of our clients have heard it's impossible to fix their status because they have a permanent bar. But what many people don't know is that there could be ways. For example, if you're married to or divorced from a U.S. citizen or resident, or you have adult U.S. citizen children, there's a case called VAWA where, depending on your relationship with that person, you could fix your status. Another potential way is the T Visa, based on abuse at work, abuse by a coyote when entering the country, or abuse in the home. And no matter how long ago it happened, you could still qualify, in many cases even if the only evidence you have is your word. So don't lose faith. Even with a permanent bar, there could be potential ways to fix your papers and secure your future in the United States.

editorial_score.why: Highly relevant to Spanish-speaking audience facing permanent bars with specific humanitarian relief pathways, but execution suffers from poor spelling/grammar and cluttered presentation.
editorial_score.check: Verify claims that VAWA applies to divorced persons and that T visa qualifies based solely on 'your word' as evidence; check ethical compliance on encouraging reliance on weak evidence claims.

creatives.transcript_en: I came in '95 and since I wasn't here legally, it was always hard for me to think about going back to my homeland, to my town. I missed my people, my family. So I went back there, I was there for a while. In '98 when I crossed, it took me 1 month to get across the border. I got caught, pushed back, and it was like a trauma for me. I was turned away by a lot of lawyers because I had no way of getting anything, so... And they told you this because you were caught at the border? Yes. I would explain my reason to them and they'd tell me, you don't qualify for anything, no way at all. So my mom died in 2012 and I couldn't go see her, and that's what really hurt me a lot, because I always felt this helplessness of not being able to even think about when I'd be able to go back. And my kids were being born... I'd say, how am I going to leave them? What documents have you gotten with us so far? Well, since I started with you all, I came to pick up my work permit and my Social Security. Sonia received her work permit, her Social Security, and we're waiting... What else are we waiting for? Supposedly the residency is on its way. The residency. Yes. And so! That first time, what are you going to do with your residency? I say that once I get that residency, I want to go to the ranch where I'm from. Uh-huh. Your homeland? You want to visit your country, right? My country. I want to go and see my relatives there, the last ones I have left there. And a question for you: do you have your work permit here with you right now? The card. I took pictures of it on my phone. Oh! Great. Let's take the picture. I have good news for you. Tell me. Okay, look. You see what it says here? What does that mean? That's your travel permit to travel outside the country and come back while we wait for your residency. Really? Oh my God, well, just imagine, that's a blessing from God. Right now I'm a person who feels really happy, grateful to you, to God, and, uh, to your whole team that helps and works for you.

creatives.headline: ¡Llámenos Hoy!
creatives.copy: ¿Quiere visitar a su familia en su país de origen? ¡No pierda más tiempo! 🤩 Abundio creía que era imposible lograrlo, pero con la ayuda de nuestro equipo hoy tiene su permiso de viaje para volver después de años. ¡Merece sentir esta misma felicidad! Llámenos YA 📞 800-259-5555.
creatives.copy_en: Do you want to visit your family in your home country? Don't waste any more time! 🤩 Abundio believed it was impossible, but with our team's help, today he has his travel permit to go back after years. You deserve to feel this same happiness! Call us NOW 📞 800-259-5555.
creatives.transcript: Vine en el 95 y por no estar legalmente, pues me costó siempre pensar en regresar a mi tierra A mi pueblo. Mirara la gente de familia entonces yo regresé allá estuve un tiempo En 98 cuando pase duré 1 mes para pasar po rla frontera Fue agarrado, aventado para atrás y fue como un trauma para mí. Yo fui rechazada por muchos abogados porque yo no tenía forma de lograr nada entonces... ¿Y ellos le dijeron esto a usted porque fue agarrao en la fronterera? Sí…yo les explicaba mi motivo si me decían que pues sabes qué No calificas ninguna forma Entonces, mi mamá muere en el 2012. Este... pues no pude ir a verla y eso fue lo que sí me dolió mucho porque sentí siempre una impotencia de no poder pensar que iba ir pero ni iba poder regresar Y mis niños estaban naciendo Digo ¿Cómo los voy dejar? Qué documentos ha ganado ya con nosotros Bueno pues como ustedes cuando empecé Vine a traer mi permiso de trabajo y el seguro. Ya recibió su permiso de trabajo, sus seguros sociales ¿Qué más estamos esperando? Supuestamente camino para la residencia La residencia Y qué es lo primero que va hacer con esa residencia Yo digo que agarrando esa residency quiero ir al ranchero donde yo vengo ¿Quiere visitar a su país? A mi país. Quiero ir y ver mis familiares, los últimos que me quedan ahí Y una pregunta para usted Usted tiene su permiso de trabajo aquí con usted en este momento La tarjeta En el teléfono le saqué fotos ¡Ah qué bueno! Vamos hacer la foto Yo tengo buenas noticias para usted Dígame Miren. Usted vea como dice aquí, Served as advanced parole ¿Eso qué significa? Eso es su permiso de viaje para viajar fuera del país y regresar mientras esperamos su residencia De veras Oh Dios mío no Pues imagínense pues eso es una bendición ¡De dios! Soy una persona ahorita me siento bien feliz agradecido con usted con Dios y con todo su equipo, le ayuda que trabaje por usted.
creatives.transcript_en: I came in '95 and since I wasn't here legally, it was always hard for me to think about going back to my homeland, to my town. To see my family, so I went back there, I was there for a while. In '98 when I crossed, it took me 1 month to get across the border. I was caught, thrown back, and it was like a trauma for me. I was turned away by a lot of lawyers because I had no way of getting anything done, so... And they told you this because you were caught at the border? Yes... I would explain my reason and they would tell me, well, you know what, you don't qualify in any way. Then my mom died in 2012. Um... well, I couldn't go see her and that's what really hurt me a lot, because I always felt so powerless, not being able to think about going, because I wouldn't be able to come back. And my kids were being born. I said, how am I going to leave them? What documents have you won with us so far? Well, like you all, when I started, I came to get my work permit and my social security. You've already received your work permit, your social security. What else are we waiting for? Supposedly on the way to residency. Residency. And what's the first thing you're going to do with that residency? I say that once I get that residency, I want to go to the ranch where I come from. You want to visit your country? My country. I want to go and see my relatives, the last ones I have left there. And a question for you: do you have your work permit here with you right now? The card. I took pictures of it on my phone. Oh, great! Let's take the photo. I have good news for you. Tell me. Look. You see how it says here, Served as advanced parole? What does that mean? That's your travel permit to travel outside the country and come back while we wait for your residency. Really? Oh my God, no. Well, imagine that, that's a blessing. From God! I'm a person who right now feels very happy, grateful to you, to God, and to your whole team that helps you and works for you.

editorial_score.why: Real client (Abundio) tells his own story on camera, attorney beside him; documentary b-roll; natural and believable, the style Ed prefers.
editorial_score.check: Testimonial use requires client consent; outcome (travel permission) is case-specific. Disclaimer shown.

creatives.transcript: Tres maneras de arreglar papeles sin tener hijos o esposos y de raro.
creatives.transcript_en: Three ways to fix your papers without having children or spouses, and of rare.

editorial_score.why: The hook addresses a real pain point (fixing status without family ties) but the CTA is just 'follow us' with no immediate consultation offer or concrete path forward.
editorial_score.check: Phrase 'arreglar papeles' is culturally appropriate but verify the promised content actually delivers three specific pathways and doesn't promise outcomes beyond legal representation.

creatives.hook: Mi nombre es Ángeles Sinti, soy abogada de inmigración y me encanta mi trabajo porque en mi firma arreglamos a personas que han escuchado muchas veces los otros avogados que no calificaban para nada.
creatives.hook_en: My name is Ángeles Sinti, I'm an immigration attorney, and I love my job because at my firm we fix papers for people who have heard many times from other attorneys that they didn't qualify for anything.
creatives.copy: ¿Le han dicho que no califica para sus papeles? 🤔 ¡No se rinda! Únase a nuestra comunidad para descubrir cómo conseguir un estatus legal, sin salir del país. ¡Siga nuestra página para no perderse más oportunidades! ✨
creatives.copy_en: Have you been told you don't qualify for your papers? 🤔 Don't give up! Join our community to discover how to get legal status without leaving the country. Follow our page so you don't miss any more opportunities! ✨
creatives.transcript: Mi nombre es Ángeles Sinti, soy abogada de inmigración y me encanta mi trabajo porque en mi firma arreglamos a personas que han escuchado muchas veces los otros avogados que no calificaban para nada. A nuestros clientes usualmente tiene como más una entrada por ejemplo sin permiso o tal vez han sido deportados Han sido agarrados e la frontera Y por eso los otro dicen qué No hay manera De arreglar Los papele Pero gracias Adios Si Hay maneras Con casos Diferentes Que se llaman Caso Humanitario y en mi firma tenemos mucha experiencia usando estos casos para arreglar a personas con deportaciones, agarradas muchas entradas otras cosas. Y arreglamos sin tener que salir de los Estados Unidos
creatives.transcript_en: My name is Ángeles Sinti, I'm an immigration attorney, and I love my job because at my firm we get papers for people who have heard many times from other lawyers that they didn't qualify for anything. Our clients usually have, for example, more than one entry without permission, or maybe they've been deported, or they've been caught at the border. And that's why others say there's no way to fix their papers. But thank God, yes, there are ways, with different cases called humanitarian cases, and at my firm we have a lot of experience using these cases to get papers for people with deportations, border apprehensions, multiple entries, and other things. And we fix their status without them having to leave the United States

editorial_score.why: Strongly relevant to a specific underserved audience (those told they don't qualify, with deportations/unlawful entries) and attorney directly addresses their pain point, but CTA is weak (follow page) and execution suffers from captioning issues and unclear framing.
editorial_score.check: Check claim that firm can fix cases 'without leaving the US' for people with deportations/multiple entries—may overstate eligibility for adjustment vs. consular processing and could mislead clients about complex waiver requirements.

creatives.copy:
¿Tiene castigo permanente en su récord migratorio? Algunas personas piensan que eso significa que no hay solución, pero en Lisinski Law Firm sabemos que muchos casos requieren revisar todas las posibilidades antes de rendirse.
Nuestro equipo trabaja para encontrar opciones incluso en situaciones complejas.

Llame ahora.

creatives.copy_en:
Do you have a permanent bar on your immigration record? Some people think that means there's no solution, but at Lisinski Law Firm we know many cases require reviewing every possibility before giving up.
Our team works to find options even in complex situations.
Find out what could be possible in your situation.
Call now.

creatives.transcript: Soy abogada de inmigración y casi cada día nos llaman personas que tienen castigo permanente Y nos dicen lo mismo que otros le han dicho que es imposible arreglar teniendo esto. Es una gran lástima tantísimos abogados dicen eso porque en realidad hay maneras Usualmente tiene usar un caso humanitario, porque estos casos tienen pertones muy fuertes reglas más flexibles Pero me encantan porqué con esos casos puede arreglar aquí dentro No tiene salir ni recomendaciones que nos llame solo para ver, y vamos a hacer todo lo que podemos para ayudarle.
creatives.transcript_en: I'm an immigration attorney, and almost every day people call us who have the permanent bar and tell us the same thing others have told them, that it's impossible to fix with that. It's a real shame so many attorneys say that, because in reality there are ways. Usually you have to use a humanitarian case, because these cases have very strong waivers and more flexible rules. But I love them because with these cases you can fix right here inside, you don't have to leave. I recommend you call us just to see, and we'll do everything we can to help you.

editorial_score.why: Speaks to people told a permanent bar ('castigo permanente') means no options; attorney on camera, conversational, hedged ('usualmente', 'hay maneras').
editorial_score.check: Must not imply every barred person qualifies; humanitarian route needs case-by-case review.

creatives.copy: ¿Pensando en salir del país para arreglar? ✈️ Podría no ser necesario 💪 No pierda la fe, nuestro equipo podría ayudarle 📞

creatives.transcript: Muchas personas se han ido y no han podido regresar porque les negaron el caso por una razón u otra cuando estaban en su país. Entonces, ¿por qué tomar el riesgo de salir si NO es necesario? Si usted califica para VAWA No tiene que tomar ese riesgo ,no tiene que salir .No tiene esperar años Y años Años Puede arreglar muy rápido Seguramente aquí estados unidos ¿Por qué no hacer esto?
creatives.transcript_en: Many people have left and haven't been able to come back because their case was denied for one reason or another while they were in their home country. So why take the risk of leaving if it's NOT necessary? If you qualify for VAWA, you don't have to take that risk, you don't have to leave. You don't have to wait years and years and years. You can fix your status very quickly, safely, here in the United States. Why not do this?

editorial_score.why: Highly specific message to undocumented people considering consular processing who may qualify for VAWA, with a fear-based hook about denial risk, but CTA is generic and credibility relies only on attorney presence.
editorial_score.check: Verify no outcome promises around 'muy rápido' (very quickly) and that VAWA eligibility screening is thorough—ad implies ease without showing qualifications or disclaimers.

creatives.hook: ¿Sólo puede calificar para BAWA por abuso extremo?
creatives.hook_en: Can you only qualify for BAWA for extreme abuse?
creatives.headline: ¡Llámenos!
creatives.copy: ¿Es cierto que solo puede calificar para VAWA con un reporte policial? 🚨 No deje que los mitos sobre VAWA lo detengan—hable con un abogado con experiencia en casos humanitarios para conocer todas las opciones potenciales. ¡Llámenos YA! 📞 800-259-5555
creatives.copy_en: Is it true you can only qualify for VAWA with a police report? 🚨 Don't let myths about VAWA stop you—talk to an attorney with experience in humanitarian cases to learn all your potential options. Call us NOW! 📞 800-259-5555
creatives.transcript: ¿Sólo puede calificar para BAWA por abuso extremo? Mito tiene que demostrar que sufrió abusos extremos para arreglar con BAWA. Realidad, bajo el caso de Bawa podría calificar basándose en abusas físicos verbal económico o psicológica O emocional no necesita un reporte policial sobre los hechos Tome control del futuro y llámenlos Subtítulos realizados por la comunidad de Amara.org
creatives.transcript_en: Can you only qualify for VAWA because of extreme abuse? Myth: you have to prove you suffered extreme abuse to fix your status with VAWA. Reality: under a VAWA case you could qualify based on physical, verbal, financial, psychological, or emotional abuse. You don't need a police report about what happened. Take control of your future and call us Subtitles by the Amara.org community

editorial_score.why: Addresses a very specific VAWA misconception (police report requirement) that likely stops victims from seeking help, with a clear myth-busting format and direct call to action.
editorial_score.check: Verify that statement 'you don't need a police report' doesn't oversimplify VAWA eligibility or create false expectations about documentation requirements.

creatives.transcript: Saludos a todos, Labras Abogada de inmigración, Francia Sarroyo, soy experta certificada en la SES de inmigración por la barra de abogados de California. Quería hablarles y comunicarles de lo que está pasando en los Estados Unidos en este momento. Quiero que me escuchen bien. Estamos en una administración que está bien enfocada en enforzar las leyes que tienen en los libros. Las leyes de deportación tratar de cambiar leyes para deportar a más personas y quitar ciertos beneficios. Ahora, como experta en las leyes de inmigración, les puedo comunicar, informar que no ha cambiado mucho. Dentro del bufete de inmigración, aquí en Los años de Cigo Alvigates, estamos viendo aprobaciones de asilo de la Corte, que hemos tenido, creo que, dos en las últimas dos semanas, aprobaciones de permiso de trabajo, residencias, entre otras cosas. Uno de los casos que hace poco tuvimos aprobado fue una orden de deportación que fue reabierta por el juez de inmigración en Texas. Imagínense, una orden de deportación abierta, una reapertura de una orden de deportación de un juez de Texas. Tengo los estados más conservadores que hay. ¿Cuál es el mensaje? El mensaje es que todos los beneficios de inmigración, casi todos, todavía existen. No ha cambiado ninguna ley. Han entrado más personas de ICE, han entrado más odio de parte de esta administración, pero dentro de lo que es la práctica de inmigración, todavía estamos practicando inmigración, todavía tenemos aprobaciones y estamos ayudando a muchas personas. Así que estamos viendo las noticias, asustamos, quizás, apague en la televisión y escuchen a los expertos en inmigración que les van a comunicar y les vamos a comunicar lo pertinente y lo relevante. Si hay algo que se debe comunicar, del cual va a afectar a los inmigrantes o a algún proceso migrator específico, no cabe duda que yo voy a hacer la primera en reportarla. Ahora no voy a hacer la abogada, que voy a reportar cada noticia, cada pequeño cambio propuesto. ¿Por qué? Porque lo que estamos viendo es que todas las maneras de esta administración de tratar de cambiar y dañar los procesos migratorios no han llegado a nada. Las cortes lo han parado todo. ¿Por qué? Porque como habíamos hablado, todo esto es anticonstitucional. Así que no pierdan la fe, continúen sus procesos, eso es lo que ellos quieren. Quitarle las ganas de seguir, meterle miedo para que las personas se vayan del país o no continúen con sus procesos migratorios. Recuérdense que al final del día, un proceso migratorio que nos encamina a legalización, a una residencia, eventualmente también a una ciudadanía, empodera a nuestra comunidad. ¿Por qué? Porque seremos votantes. Y ese es el punto de todo esto, es meterle mano, tener valentía y nosotros somos responsables de los transportes propiedad. Tenemos que tomar pasos masivos para ver efectos y cambios masivos en nuestras vidas. Así que al fin del día, no tengan miedo, informense bien y vengan a hablar con los expertos de la ley de migración. Aquí los esperamos.
creatives.transcript_en: Saludos to all the French immigration lawyer, I am an expert certified in immigration law by California's lawyer bar. I wanted to talk to you and tell you about what is happening in the United States at the moment. I want you to listen to me well. We are an administration that is well focused on enforcing laws that are in the books. We are trying to change laws to deport more people and remove certain benefits. Now, as an expert in immigration law, I can tell you that it has not changed much. Within immigration buffets, here in the years of Stigo Arvquets, we are seeing court asylum approvals, I think it was two weeks ago, work permits, residences, among other things. One of the cases that we had recently approved was a deportation order that was reopened by the immigration judge in Texas. Imagine an open deportation order, a reopening of a deportation order from a Texas judge. I think it is one of the most conservative states there is. What is the message? The message is that all the benefits of immigration, almost all, still exist. No law has changed. More people have entered ICE, more hate has entered this administration. But within immigration practice, we are still practicing immigration, we still have approvals and we are helping many people. So we are seeing the news, we are not afraid, maybe they turn off the TV and listen to the immigration experts who are going to communicate and we are going to communicate the relevant and relevant. If there is something that should be communicated that will affect immigrants or some specific immigration process, there is no doubt that I am going to report it first. Now I am not going to report every news, every small change, why? Because what we are seeing is that all the ways of this administration, of trying to change and damage the immigration processes, have not reached anything. The courts have stopped everything. Why? Because as we have talked about, all this is anti-constitutional. So, do not lose faith, continue your processes, that is what they want. Take away the desire to continue, to get scared so that people leave the country or not continue with their mandatory processes. Remember that at the end of the day, a mandatory process that encams us on legalization, a residence, eventually also a citizenship, empowers our community. Why? Because we will be voters. And that is the point of all this, is to get your hands on it, have courage and we are responsible for our own lives. We have to take massive steps to see effects and massive changes in our lives. So, at the end of the day, do not be afraid, inform yourself and come to talk to the experts in immigration. Here we wait.

creatives.copy:
⚠️ Facing deportation does not automatically mean your case is over. Immigration Court may still offer defenses, but preparation and timing matter.

Being placed in removal proceedings means the government is asking an Immigration Judge to determine whether you should be removed from the United States. It does not mean deportation happens automatically. Depending on your history and circumstances, you may have legal defenses or forms of relief available.

Possible options may include:

✓ Asylum
✓ Cancellation of Removal
✓ Adjustment of Status when legally available
✓ Immigration waivers
✓ Motions or appeals
✓ Other forms of relief based on your individual case

⚖️ A strong removal defense requires more than showing up to court.

Your attorney may need to review your Notice to Appear, immigration history, prior applications, criminal record, family circumstances, and every potential form of relief. Supporting evidence, consistent testimony, and strict compliance with Immigration Court deadlines can all become critical.

One of the biggest mistakes is waiting until shortly before the hearing to build a defense. Missing an available form of relief or failing to present the right evidence can have serious consequences.

With 18 years of immigration law experience, attorney Alena Shautsova represents clients in removal proceedings, asylum matters, cancellation of removal, waivers, motions, and BIA appeals.

creatives.copy:
😰¿Estás ahogado en deudas y te dijeron que la insolvencia económica es ilegal?

🚨Así como han hecho muchas personas inescrupulosas con el SOAT que no es ilegal, la ley de insolvencia tampoco.

👉🏼Son leyes creadas para proteger, no para hacer fraude.
Lo ilegal es usarlas con mala fe.

📌Si tus deudas son reales y no tienes cómo salir, la ley existe para darte una segunda oportunidad.
creatives.copy_en:
😰Are you drowning in debt and were told that economic insolvency is illegal?

🚨Just like many unscrupulous people have done with SOAT which is not illegal, the insolvency law isn't either.

👉🏼These are laws created to protect, not to commit fraud.
What's illegal is using them in bad faith.

📌If your debts are real and you have no way out, the law exists to give you a second chance.
creatives.transcript: Abogada, tengo muchas deudas. Ahora con todo lo que se ha destapado del cartel de la insolvencia hoy en día ¿la insolvencia es legal? Me llegó este mensaje y voy a ser muy clara No! La Insolvenia Económica no es ilegal Y te voy explicar como un ejemplo que todos tenemos El SOA Todos sabemos qué el SOAP Es seguro obligatorio Que funciona para atender A las víctimas De accidentes Del tránsito Una ley noble Necesaria Que protege vida Pero miren Lo qué pasó Personas inescrupulosos empezaron a usar el SOA para lo que no era. Hacían pasar cualquier tipo de accidente como si fuese un accidente de tránsito, accidentes domésticos o caída en la casa hasta lesiones que nada tenían qué ver con vehículos ¿Y para qué? Para cobrar seguros fraudulentamente Y ahí se metieron médico corruptores dueños ambulancias ciudadanitos mal afectados haciendo negocios por algo nacido para ayudar Acaso esto volvió ilegal No, el SOA sigue siendo vigente necesario y totalmente legal. Lo que es ilegal es el uso corrupto que algunos les están dando tal cual como lo está pasando con la ley de insolvencia Una ley noble creada para dar una segunda oportunidad a personas quedaron ahogadas en deudas sin mala fe Esa leyes completamente legales Y esta vigente Pero abogados corruptos Centros De Conciliación Tramposo y personas que sacaron créditos sabiendo que no los pueden pagar, convirtieron la ley en un negocio sucio. Pero que quede claro La Ley de Insolvencia NO ES ILLEGAL Entonces si usted tiene deudas reales Y está sufriendo acoso a bancos o casas del cobro Si siente qué No Tiene Salida LA LEY ESTÁ DE SU LADO Soy Daniela Bogada Bogadá Que Sabe Lo Qué Los Demás ¡No Saben!
creatives.transcript_en: Lawyer, I have a lot of debts. Now with everything that's come out about the insolvency cartel today, is insolvency legal? I got this message and I'm going to be very clear. No! Economic Insolvency is not illegal. And I'll explain it with an example we all know. SOAT. Everyone knows that SOAT is mandatory insurance that works to attend to victims of traffic accidents. A noble law. Necessary. That protects life. But look what happened. Unscrupulous people started using SOAT for what it wasn't for. They passed off any type of accident as if it were a traffic accident, domestic accidents or falls at home, even injuries that had nothing to do with vehicles. And for what? To fraudulently collect insurance. And that's where corrupt doctors got involved, ambulance owners, bad-intentioned citizens doing business with something born to help. Did this make it illegal? No, SOAT is still current, necessary and totally legal. What's illegal is the corrupt use that some are giving it, just like what's happening with the insolvency law. A noble law created to give a second chance to people who are drowning in debt without bad faith. That law is completely legal and is in effect. But corrupt lawyers, shady conciliation centers, and people who took out loans knowing they couldn't pay them turned the law into a dirty business. But let's be clear. The Insolvency Law IS NOT ILLEGAL. So if you have real debts and are suffering harassment from banks or collection agencies, if you feel like you have no way out, THE LAW IS ON YOUR SIDE. I'm Daniela Bogada. A Lawyer Who Knows What Others Don't Know!

editorial_score.check: This is not a US immigration ad—it promotes Colombian bankruptcy/insolvency law services; do not adapt for US immigration marketing.

creatives.copy:
⚠️ ¿Firmaste como fiador o codeudor?

👉🏼Te pueden embargar.

💡¿Aplica la insolvencia? Sí puede aplicar, incluso siendo codeudor. Pero ojo: solo lo protege a usted, no al deudor.

📌 Moraleja:
Firmar es responder.
Y responder puede costarte tu casa, su carro o tu tranquilidad.
creatives.copy_en:
⚠️ Did you sign as a guarantor or co-debtor?

👉🏼 They can garnish you.

💡 Does insolvency apply? Yes, it can apply, even as a co-debtor. But watch out: it only protects you, not the debtor.

📌 Moral of the story:
Signing means being liable.

creatives.transcript: ¿Pueden embargar al codeudor o fiador y éste se puede acoger a la ley de insolvencia? Te explico qué pasa en Colombia. Primero, sí pueden embargar al codeudoro fiado Cuando usted firma como codeudo lo trata como si usted fuera el deuedor principal Que le pueden embargara cuentas bancarias Su casa Tu carro Y hasta una parte su salario Si gana más que un mínimo Qué no les puedan embarga El salario mínimo Sus prestaciones Lo indispensable para vivir Como utensilios cocinas O herramientos del trabajo Segundo, sí puede acogerse a la ley de insolvencia. La ley aplica tanto para deudores principales como para codeudores y fiadores Usted puede solicitar el proceso de insolvencia si está ahogado en deudas De buena fe ¡Ojo! Pero Si usted se Acoge Insoluencia eso no libera automáticamente al Doudore principal Ni los otros Codeudores Usted Se Proteje Pero para que los demás nos sigan expuestos tiene que quedar estipulado En El Acuerdo Insólito ¿Qué hacer? Si ya te notificaron un embargo, no te quedes quieto. Busca a una abogado especializado Revisa si puedes demostrar que actuaste de buena fe Y sí califica inicia el proceso De insolvencia La oportunidad también existe para fiadores y codeudores honestos Soy Daniela Abogada la Abogada que sabe los demás No saben
creatives.transcript_en: Can a co-debtor or guarantor be garnished, and can they file for insolvency? I'll explain what happens in Colombia. First, yes, they can garnish the co-debtor or guarantor. When you sign as a co-debtor, they treat you as if you were the main debtor. What they can garnish: Your bank accounts. Your house. Your car. And even part of your salary if you earn more than minimum wage. What they cannot garnish: Minimum wage. Your benefits. What's essential to live. Like kitchen utensils or work tools. Second, yes, you can file for insolvency. The law applies to both primary debtors and co-debtors and guarantors. You can request the insolvency process if you're drowning in debt. In good faith. Watch out! But if you file for insolvency, that doesn't automatically release the main debtor or the other co-debtors. You protect yourself. But for the others not to remain exposed, it has to be stipulated in the insolvency agreement. What to do? If you've already been notified of a garnishment, don't just sit there. Find a specialized lawyer. Check if you can prove you acted in good faith. And if you qualify, start the insolvency process. The opportunity also exists for honest guarantors and co-debtors. I'm Daniela, the lawyer who knows what others don't know.

Green Card without leaving the U.S. (T Visa) | DO YOU WANT A GREEN CARD WITHOUT LEAVING THE UNITED STATES? 🇺🇸💥

If you suffered labor exploitation or were forced to work when you were a minor, you could qualify for the T Visa, an immigration option that lets you adjust status without leaving the country… and petition for your immediate family members!

🔹 Were you forced to work when you were a minor?
🔹 Did you have to care for children, clean houses, or work in the fields long hours without fair pay?
🔹 Did your partner control you with threats or take your money?
🔹 Were you brought to the U.S. with false promises of work or studies?

If you answered YES to any of these questions, you could be eligible.

👉 The T Visa includes immigration waivers for people with entries without permission, previous deportations, or even criminal records related to your situation.
👉 It also allows you to include your children, partner, or parents within your application, regardless of whether they are inside or outside the country.

💡Many immigrants have a strong case and don't know it — because nobody explained it to them well.

creatives.copy_en:
Looking to build your future in the United States?

The EB-2 National Interest Waiver program is helping qualified professionals obtain permanent residence.

With limited visas and growing demand, reviewing your profile right now can save you years of waiting.

I'm Carlos Colombo, an immigration attorney with over 25 years of experience.

For many years, my team and I have helped thousands of professionals obtain approvals for permanent residence in the United States.

One of the most powerful ways to make this a reality is through the EB-2 National Interest Waiver.

This program allows certain highly qualified professionals to apply for a green card on their own, without needing a U.S. employer to sponsor them.

But here's the challenge: I've seen many professionals wait for the "perfect moment" to apply.

And while they wait, others with similar profiles are already filing their cases and securing their place in line.

That matters, because the number of visas is limited.

The longer you delay, the greater the risk that requirements will become stricter and wait times will be longer.

I know it's normal to want more savings, more professional achievements, or more certainty before starting.

But in my experience, I've seen time and again that waiting generally makes the process harder, not easier.

Right now conditions remain favorable.

That can end.

If you want to explore whether the EB-2 National Interest Waiver is a good option for you, click below to get a free evaluation.

It may be the best step you take toward your future in the United States.

creatives.transcript_en: Would you like to know how to get permanent residency in the United States? Most visa options require an employer willing to sponsor you, or winning a lottery and even investing close to 1 million. But there is another alternative designed for professionals with a university degree OR postgraduate studies. It's the EB2 national interest. And today I want to explain to you how it works. I'm Carlos Colombo, immigration attorney with over 25 years of experience. For many years my team and I have helped thousands of professionals obtain approvals for permanent residency in the United States. Engineers, doctors, technology specialists, and other professionals from diverse areas. As an immigrant, I perfectly understand your situation and what it means to achieve the so-called American dream. That's why today I want to tell you how this alternative works and how it can be your opportunity to advance your immigration goals. So what makes the EB2 national interest different from other options to obtain residency in the United States? Well, there are three advantages that really make the difference. First, you don't need an employer to sponsor you. You file your own petition. This means you maintain control of your entire immigration process, you don't depend on whether a company can change jobs freely or start your own business. Your path to permanent residency continues regardless of your employment situation. Second, you don't need to make a large investment. Unlike visas designed for investors that require hundreds of thousands or even a million, the EB2 national interest is based mostly on your professional trajectory and credentials. And third, it doesn't require labor certification. This is very key because it reduces the complexity of the process compared to employer-sponsored routes. Also, your case is evaluated on merit, not by lottery or chance. This is what I want to offer you today. A free evaluation with no obligation of your professional profile. We're going to analyze your academic background, your experience, and your fields to determine if the EB2 national interest visa is right for you. Don't wait any longer. Processing times keep increasing as each month more professionals are filing their applications. The question isn't whether you should or shouldn't pursue permanent residency in the United States, the real question is when are you going to start? Request your free professional profile evaluation today. Share your resume or professional profile by leaving a call with our team. We'll analyze your trajectory, your situation, and give you an evaluation about the EB2 national interest. This evaluation is completely confidential and without any obligation. Your path to permanent residency in the United States begins with clarity about your options. I hope to be able to accompany you and be your ally in this important transition.

creatives.headline_en: Experts in Green Card for the EB-2 National Interest Visa
creatives.copy:
Existe una vía para obtener la residencia permanente en los Estados Unidos, sin necesidad de patrocinio de un empleador ni una inversión millonaria.

La EB-2 por Interés Nacional, y está diseñada para profesionales altamente calificados.

Su educación y su experiencia pueden convertirse en la base del futuro de su familia en los Estados Unidos.

Más que una oportunidad, la EB-2 por interés nacional representa estabilidad y tranquilidad para usted y sus seres queridos.

A continuación, le explico cómo funciona.

Permítame poner la EB-2 NIW en contexto con respecto a otras alternativas para obtener la residencia permanente en los Estados Unidos u otras visas.

La visa H-1B, por ejemplo, es un sistema de lotería.

Su asignación es por azar.

Y usted depende completamente de su empleador y no es aplicación a residencia permanente.

Por otro lado, la visa de inversionista EB-5 requiere una inversión alta de entre 800,000 a 1.5 millones de dólares.

Por eso la EB-2 por interés nacional es diferente.

Porque es una vía en la que:

No necesita un empleador que lo patrocine.

Usted presenta su propia petición.

No necesita invertir cientos o miles o millones de dólares.

Su experiencia profesional es su calificación y no depende de una lotería.

Su caso se evalúa, mayormente, por sus méritos.

Y si está considerando esta vía, ahora es un momento clave para comenzar.

Le explico por qué.

Estamos viendo más profesionales que nunca iniciar su solicitud para la visa EB-2 por interés nacional.

A medida que aumenta la demanda, los tiempos de procesamiento se están viendo afectados.

Lo que antes tomaba alrededor de dos años, ahora puede extenderse hasta cinco años en algunas categorías.

He visto a muchos profesionales esperar el “momento perfecto” para aplicar y mientras esperan otros con perfiles similares ya están presentando sus casos y asegurando su lugar en la fila.

Pero la realidad es esta:

Hay profesionales que no esperaron y que presentaron su solicitud hace menos de dos años, y ya están en la instancia de revisión de su caso.

Aquí es donde Colombo & Hurd puede ayudarle.

Desde 2023, hemos acompañado a más de 2,500 profesionales en la preparación y aprobación exitosa de sus solicitudes EB-2 por interés nacional.

Nuestro enfoque es colaborativo.

Usted aporta su experiencia y sus logros profesionales.

Nosotros aportamos nuestro conocimiento en leyes de inmigración y la estrategia necesaria para presentar su caso de la mejor manera posible, la más sólida y convincente posible.

Esto es lo que quiero ofrecerle hoy:

Una evaluación gratuita y sin compromiso de su perfil profesional.

Vamos a analizar su formación académica, su experiencia y su campo de trabajo para determinar si la visa EB-2 por interés nacional es adecuada para usted.

Espero poder acompañarlo y ser su aliado en esta importante transición.
creatives.copy_en:
There is a path to get permanent residency in the United States, without needing an employer sponsor or a million-dollar investment.

The EB-2 National Interest, and it's designed for highly qualified professionals.

Your education and your experience can become the foundation of your family's future in the United States.

More than an opportunity, the EB-2 national interest represents stability and peace of mind for you and your loved ones.

Below, I'll explain how it works.

Let me put the EB-2 NIW in context with respect to other alternatives to obtain permanent residency in the United States or other visas.

The H-1B visa, for example, is a lottery system.

Its assignment is by chance.

And you depend completely on your employer and it is not an application for permanent residency.

On the other hand, the EB-5 investor visa requires a high investment of between 800,000 to 1.5 million dollars.

That's why the EB-2 national interest is different.

Because it is a path in which:

You don't need an employer to sponsor you.

You file your own petition.

You don't need to invest hundreds or thousands or millions of dollars.

Your professional experience is your qualification and it doesn't depend on a lottery.

Your case is evaluated, mostly, on your merits.

And if you are considering this path, now is a key moment to begin.

I'll explain why.

We are seeing more professionals than ever start their application for the EB-2 national interest visa.

As demand increases, processing times are being affected.

What used to take around two years, can now extend up to five years in some categories.

I have seen many professionals wait for the "perfect moment" to apply and while they wait others with similar profiles are already filing their cases and securing their place in line.

But the reality is this:

There are professionals who didn't wait and who filed their application less than two years ago, and are already at the review stage of their case.

This is where Colombo & Hurd can help you.

Since 2023, we have accompanied more than 2,500 professionals in the preparation and successful approval of their EB-2 national interest applications.

Our approach is collaborative.

You bring your experience and your professional achievements.

We bring our knowledge in immigration law and the strategy needed to present your case in the best possible way, the most solid and convincing possible.

This is what I want to offer you today:

A free evaluation with no obligation of your professional profile.

We are going to analyze your academic background, your experience and your field of work to determine if the EB-2 national interest visa is right for you.

I hope to be able to accompany you and be your ally in this important transition.

Many skilled professionals hold off on applying, waiting to hit a career milestone or find the "perfect" time. Meanwhile, others are already moving forward and securing their place in line. 

The EB-2 NIW (National Interest Waiver) allows advanced degree holders to pursue a U.S. green card without needing an employer sponsor, giving you the freedom to build your career on your own terms. 

We've helped over 2,500 professionals secure green card approvals through EB-2 NIW since 2023. But conditions can shift, and delaying your application, even by a few months, can push back your entire timeline. 

If you're a skilled professional considering your options, don't wait for a "perfect moment" that may never come. Get a complimentary case evaluation today and find out if EB-2 NIW is right for you.

Expertos en Green Card para la Visa de Interés Nacional EB-2 | Cada vez son más los profesionales con educación profesional avanzada los que solicitan la residencia en los Estados Unidos vía la EB-2 por interés nacional. 

Pero con el número de visas disponibles limitado se espera que el proceso lleve más tiempo de lo habitual. 

Si usted es un profesional calificado que planea mudarse a los Estados Unidos, es una buena idea solicitar la revisión de su perfil EB-2 interés nacional lo antes posible.

Soy Carlos Colombo, abogado de inmigración con más de 25 años de experiencia. 

Por muchos años, mi equipo y yo ayudamos a miles de profesionales a obtener aprobaciones para la residencia permanente en los Estados Unidos.

Una de las formas más poderosas de hacer esto realidad es a través de la EB-2 por interés nacional.

Este programa le permite a ciertos profesionales altamente calificados a solicitar una green card por cuenta propia, sin necesidad de que un empleador americano lo pida.

Pero aquí está el desafío: he visto a muchos profesionales esperar el "momento perfecto" para aplicar. 

Y mientras esperan, otros con perfiles similares ya están presentando sus casos y asegurando su lugar en la fila.

Eso es importante, porque el número de visas es limitado. 

Cuanto más se demore, mayor va a ser el riesgo de que los requisitos sean más estrictos y los tiempos de espera sean más largos.

Sé que es normal querer conseguir más ahorros, otros logros profesionales o tener más certeza antes de comenzar. 

Pero en mi experiencia, he visto una y otra vez que esperar generalmente hace que el proceso sea más difícil, no más fácil.

En este momento las condiciones siguen siendo favorables. 

Eso se puede acabar.

Si desea explorar si la EB-2 por interés nacional es una buena opción para usted, haga clic a continuación para obtener una evaluación gratuita. 

Puede ser el mejor paso que da hacia su futuro en los Estados Unidos.
creatives.card_text_en:
Green Card Experts for the EB-2 National Interest Waiver Visa | More and more professionals with advanced professional education are applying for residency in the United States via the EB-2 national interest waiver.

But with the number of available visas limited, the process is expected to take longer than usual.

If you are a qualified professional planning to move to the United States, it's a good idea to request a review of your EB-2 national interest waiver profile as soon as possible.

I'm Carlos Colombo, an immigration attorney with over 25 years of experience.

For many years, my team and I have helped thousands of professionals obtain approvals for permanent residency in the United States.

One of the most powerful ways to make this a reality is through the EB-2 national interest waiver.

This program allows certain highly qualified professionals to apply for a green card on their own, without needing a U.S. employer to sponsor them.

But here's the challenge: I've seen many professionals wait for the "perfect moment" to apply.

And while they wait, others with similar profiles are already filing their cases and securing their place in line.

That matters, because the number of visas is limited.

The longer you delay, the greater the risk that requirements will become stricter and wait times will be longer.

I know it's normal to want to save more money, achieve more professional accomplishments, or have more certainty before starting.

But in my experience, I've seen time and time again that waiting usually makes the process harder, not easier.

Right now conditions remain favorable.

That can end.

If you want to explore whether the EB-2 national interest waiver is a good option for you, click below to get a free evaluation.

It may be the best step you take toward your future in the United States.

editorial_score.check: Verify that 'thousands of professionals' claim is substantiated and ensure 'free evaluation' doesn't create expectation of free legal advice beyond initial screening

The EB-2 NIW program is helping qualified professionals obtain permanent residency.

I have been observing a pattern among highly qualified professionals that concerns me.

While you are still waiting for the "right time" to submit your EB-2 NIW application, other professionals have already started their applications and secured their spots in line.

Why does this matter?

They realized that the longer they delay, the greater the chances that changes in the EB-2 NIW process and wait times could work against them.

All this while you are probably waiting for a new career milestone, more savings, or what seems like the "perfect moment" to start the process.

And I am here to tell you that, with the new proposed changes, NOW may be the "perfect" moment.

Having helped more than 2,000 professionals, like you, obtain approval since 2023, I have observed the impacts that waiting just one more month can have on your green card approval timeline.

Right now, current processing conditions continue to favor qualified professionals.

BUT!

With requirements possibly becoming more rigid due to higher demand and increasing approval timelines, waiting for the perfect moment will not reduce your risk.

In fact, waiting may increase the risk of facing stricter requirements and longer processing times.

Click below and secure your free EB-2 NIW evaluation before the right time becomes the wrong time.

creatives.card_text:
Boletim de Vistos: EB-2 Atual | Esta atualização pode te dar uma grande vantagem no seu processo de Green Card. 

O Boletim de Vistos de março de 2026 tornou o EB-2 “Atual” na tabela de Datas para Protocolo para a maioria dos países, criando uma oportunidade poderosa para profissionais elegíveis que estão dentro dos EUA.  

Se você estiver em status legal e tiver uma petição EB-2 aprovada, agora pode ser possível protocolar o Ajuste de Status, independentemente da data de prioridade.  

Protocolar pode significar:  

Checkmark button Autorização de trabalho não vinculada ao seu empregador  
Checkmark button Permissão para viagens internacionais 
Checkmark button Maior flexibilidade profissional no longo prazo 
Checkmark button Proteção adicional caso o EB-2 retroceda 

Os números de visto são limitados. E, quando a demanda aumenta, o status de “Atual” pode mudar. 

Na Colombo & Hurd, ajudamos mais de 2.500 profissionais a obter aprovações somente desde 2023, por meio de caminhos de Green Card sem patrocínio empregatício, como o EB-2 NIW.  

Descubra como essa atualização pode te aproximar da residência permanente. Faça hoje mesmo uma avaliação gratuita do seu perfil.

creatives.transcript_en: Did you know that the EB-2 National Interest Waiver has become the most popular visa for immigrating legally with permanent residence to the United States? Is it everyone who is a professional can get this permanent residence and it's not like that, you have to meet certain requirements. Number one you need an advanced degree. What does that mean? First of all you can have a master's degree, a doctorate, and it's important to understand this OR. You can have 1 bachelor's degree plus 5 years of professional experience which would be the equivalent of an advanced degree. Second, this part is important. A lot of people don't understand it well, it's meeting the national interest requirement. You have to have a proposal that is of national interest to the United States, has substantial merit, and you have to be positioned to be able to advance that proposal. And that requirement is where we can advise you so you understand well if you can qualify for this excellent permanent residence option. Don't risk your future and your partner's legal status over avoidable mistakes. Work with experienced professionals who know how to navigate the system right from the start.

creatives.transcript_en: Hello everyone, this is your immigration attorney Frances Arroyo speaking. I'm a certified expert in immigration law by the California State Bar. Let's talk today a little bit about residences and the biggest errors I've been seeing in these applications. First, when we're submitting our residence process, it's so important that we do it correctly with all the necessary evidence from the beginning. What I've been seeing with many cases of clients who come to me with denied residences is that these are residences that could have been approved, but they have major errors. What are these errors? First, they're trying to submit these residences when there are inadmissibility issues. What does this mean? These are problems with violations of immigration laws that perhaps make them inadmissible to get this legal permanent residence. What do we do and how do we submit these residences when we have immigration problems? Inadmissibility problems as the law calls them? Number one, it's so important to submit this residence correctly. It has to be submitted, if necessary, with a waiver from the beginning. And that's where the major error is. I'm seeing that many people are afraid to submit waivers or say that this incident occurred. For example, being caught at the border, immigration fraud, thinking that immigration simply won't notice and won't find out, counting on the immigration officer simply making some error, or maybe their lawyer tells them DON'T WORRY, I've submitted many residences like this, we don't have to show what immigration violation you have on your record, they won't find that. Incorrect! I've already had many cases which we've had to reactivate and resubmit correctly with the residence application or also a waiver. If you have immigration problems, you've been caught at the borders, if you have a criminal record, you've committed fraud that we can define during our consultation, come see us to make sure we submit these residences in a way that will get them approved and we don't have to do it again, spend all that money, that time, that's the most important thing. Submit your residence so it's approvable from the beginning. In my experience with all my residences with immigration problems, if we always do them with honesty from the beginning, we're going to succeed. Those are the people who have their residence today. If there's a solution to get your residence that way, we're going to do it correctly and always with the team that lets you know how we can correctly achieve approval of these residences. Don't submit your residences if we know we have something on our records. This is a conversation you need to have with your attorney, an honest and transparent conversation. For what? So we can move you forward and toward success. That's how we're going to make sure we do everything correctly. We'll be waiting for you here.

creatives.transcript_en: Greetings everyone, if you're talking about immigration attorney Francesa Arroyo I am a certified expert in the laws by the California Bar. La visa juvenil es un tipo de visa que permite a los menores de edad que cumplen con ciertos requisitos vivir y establecerse aquí en los Estados Unidos. creatives.transcript_en: Hi everyone, I'm attorney Laura León and today I want to talk about two stories that my clients told me this week. These two stories are very very important to share with you because it could be your story too. And based on these stories there may be a legal path for you to obtain your permanent residence in the United States. The first story is a woman who, crossing into the United States, crossed with a coyote and that coyote took advantage of her for being a woman. And she has been here in the United States more than 20 years. She has not told her story to another person. But the day I did the consultation with her, I asked her about her experiences with the coyotes. That's when she tells me that the coyote took advantage of her. Where he threatened that if she didn't give in to what he wanted, he was going to go after her family and could harm them, could kidnap them, could do many things. And obviously this woman felt she had no other option but to give in to what the coyote was telling her. In another example we see a man in another family where the man, the husband, crossing into the United States, already had his wife here. They already had a baby. And of course, his goal was to enter the United States and reunite with his wife and his baby. During the process of crossing into the United States, the coyote told him you have to drive the car. He says I don't want to drive the car. I don't want the authorities to think I'm a coyote if they stop us. The coyote threatens him. He tells him if you don't drive the car, we are going to kidnap you, we are going to ask your wife for money. We know where you come from. So you have to do what we ask. This man was forced to do what the coyote asked. If this has happened to you before, or something similar happened to you at the border where the coyotes forced you to do something you didn't want to do and threatened you, told you they could harm you, could harm your family, ask for more money, this could be a legal basis to apply for a T visa. So call us today. Tell us your story. Your story starts from the moment you enter the United States. creatives.transcript_en: Three words you need to know if you're undocumented or if you have loved ones who are undocumented. Habeas Corpus Petition super important What do you know about this remedy because what would happen if you are detained in the detention centers and the government doesn't want to let you out? Habeas Corpus Petition is the remedy where you and your attorney go to federal court and ask that the government give a valid reason for the reason that you are detained in the detention centers. The government in front of the federal court has to give a valid reason for the reasons that you are detained If the government cannot give that reason. Do you have your green card and wonder if you can now apply for American citizenship?

The rules and timelines can change. If you've been waiting to become a citizen, this may be a good time to find out if you meet the requirements and take the next step. At Fayad Law, P.C. we have helped thousands of immigrant families and we serve in Spanish in Fairfax and Northern Virginia.

Call today to speak with our team confidentially. Every case is different.

creatives.transcript_en: You're a permanent resident and you're wondering if this is a good time to apply for American citizenship. Hi, I'm Dario Alcáncer, immigration attorney in Fayetteville, and for more than 20 years we've been helping thousands of immigrant families like yours secure their future here in the United States. creatives.transcript_en: Did you know that in some cases you can ask a judge to stop your deportation and even give you a Green Card? If you're in deportation proceedings, it's easy to feel like there's no way out and that you'll be separated from your loved ones. But this is not always true. I'm attorney Dariel Cancel Fayad. Every day we help families face the immigration court process. Let's talk about how you can legally ask the judge to cancel your deportation. To qualify, you must meet three requirements. First, that your departure from the country would cause extreme hardship to a spouse, parent, or child who is a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Second, that you have lived in the United States continuously for at least 10 years before being brought to court, and third, that you have good moral character. Success depends completely on presenting a convincing case with solid evidence that meets legal requirements. A simple argument just doesn't work. But when done right, the result is transformative. creatives.transcript_en: Attorney, at a time like this, how can an immigration attorney help the Latino community? Good question. creatives.transcript: ¿Cuáles son los beneficios de meter una aplicación de VisaT? Ahora, cuando metes un caso Visa T no es necesariamente garantizado si vas a recibir la carta Buena Fe pero sin embargo ciertas personas cumplen lo elementos necesarios para ganar su caso de visite pueden ganar una carta de buena fe. Cuáles son los beneficios? Si usted tiene orden y deportación, puedes meter la visa test si te dan La carta buena se puede poner un amparo forma automática sin hacer nada más desorden ni deportación punto número dos acción definitiva sí a lo mejor no tienes órdenes deportación, pero obviamente quieres la protección contra la deportación. La carta de buena fe te puede dar un protección contra una deportación en términos acción deferida también Un beneficio con casos devisa t si le dan a carta y el accion deferida que pueden dar permiso del trabajo mientras tiempo que caso sigue pendiente como las oficinas usis ahora voy ser bien sincera con ustedes, los permisos de trabajo de visa te son muy muy atrasado. Tenemos muchos clientes que han recibido su carta buena fe pero todavía están esperando los promiso del trabajo la verdad en este punto no sé si simplemente son muy atrás o sí es mala parte della administración detrás Pero sí usted tiene una visa y ha recibida una carta buenas e irnos a recibir el permiso de trabajo, es algo que puedes platicar con su abogado de inmigración.
creatives.transcript_en: What are the benefits of filing a T Visa application? The benefits include that during the time your case is pending with USCIS offices you can receive a bona fide determination letter. Now, when you file a T Visa case it's not necessarily guaranteed whether you're going to receive the bona fide determination letter, but certain people who meet the necessary elements to win their T Visa case can obtain a bona fide determination letter. What are the benefits? If you have a deportation order, you can file the T Visa and if they give you the bona fide determination letter you can get an automatic stay without doing anything else on the deportation order. Number two, deferred action. Maybe you don't have a deportation order, but obviously you want protection against deportation. The bona fide determination letter can give you protection against deportation in terms of deferred action. Also, a benefit with T Visa cases, if they give you the letter and deferred action, they can give you a work permit while your case is still pending with USCIS offices. Now I'm going to be very honest with you, T Visa work permits are very, very delayed. We have many clients who have received their bona fide determination letter but are still waiting for their work permits. The truth is at this point I don't know if they're just very behind or if it's the bad part of the administration behind it. But if you have a T Visa and have received a bona fide determination letter and are going to receive the work permit, it's something you can discuss with your immigration attorney.

editorial_score.why: Highly targeted to T Visa applicants with detailed educational content about bona fide determinations, but the talking-head video lacks visual aids and the disclaimer overlay obscures branding.

⚠️ ADVANCE PAROLE: LAS REGLAS CAMBIARON

✈️ ¿Está pensando viajar con Advance Parole? Antes de salir de Estados Unidos, revise su historial migratorio.

Una decisión reciente de la Junta de Apelaciones de Inmigración cambió una protección legal que había existido desde 2012. En Matter of Delcarmen-Lara, la BIA determinó que una salida con Advance Parole cuenta como una “departure” para efectos de ciertas prohibiciones relacionadas con presencia ilegal, revocando Matter of Arrabally and Yerrabelly.

Esto no significa que todas las personas con Advance Parole tendrán un castigo. El análisis depende de factores como la presencia ilegal acumulada, entradas y salidas anteriores y el historial migratorio individual.

🚨 No viaje basándose únicamente en experiencias de otras personas. Su caso puede ser diferente.

📞 Llame al 310-872-5156 para una consulta GRATIS y revisión de su caso antes de tomar una decisión.

#AdvanceParole #DACA #Inmigración #ConozcaSusDerechos #LosAngelesLegalAdvocates
creatives.copy_en:
⚠️ ADVANCE PAROLE: THE RULES CHANGED

✈️ Are you thinking about traveling with Advance Parole? Before leaving the United States, review your immigration history.

A recent decision by the Board of Immigration Appeals changed a legal protection that had existed since 2012. In Matter of Delcarmen-Lara, the BIA determined that a departure with Advance Parole counts as a "departure" for purposes of certain prohibitions related to unlawful presence, overturning Matter of Arrabally and Yerrabelly.

This does not mean that all people with Advance Parole will face a penalty. The analysis depends on factors such as accumulated unlawful presence, prior entries and departures, and individual immigration history.

🚨 Do not travel based solely on other people's experiences. Your case may be different.

📞 Call 310-872-5156 for a FREE consultation and review of your case before making a decision.

#AdvanceParole #DACA #Immigration #KnowYourRights #LosAngelesLegalAdvocates

creatives.transcript_en: So, let's talk directly about the problems happening right now with immigration fraud. Immigration fraud is not necessarily just something where the person applying for an immigration benefit commits fraud in order to obtain an immigration benefit. We are seeing that immigration fraud also happens a lot when people don't know that documents of some kind have been filled out for them with lies. What does this mean? They hired a notary, maybe hired a lawyer... They don't know what was submitted, never approved the forms, or don't know what benefit they are obtaining that I would never pursue if I'm in immigration proceedings. The first thing is that we have to take responsibility and not make ourselves victims of all this that is happening. We have to be smart, we are strong and intelligent people. How? We don't fall for these immigration frauds. We review all the forms before sending. It's very important to review with your lawyer every word, every piece of information you're giving to immigration. Second, we review all the evidence, the written statements, every document sent, psychological exams. Make sure everything is correct and right because it's important to know the process we're in because eventually for most immigration processes there is an interview and that's where many people realize they have been victims of fraud by a lawyer or by a notary and that's where the problem is. Why? Because these days denied applications from USCIS can end up in Immigration Court, they refer you to an immigration judge for deportation proceedings from the country. We are now in a state of emergency where we have to defend ourselves against deportation. Let's avoid all this. First, start with a good consultation, make sure you qualify. Look for information, ask the lawyer for information as soon as the process begins, make sure you're reviewing everything that's sent and that all the evidence is correct. Third, when you have your interview it's very important that you go well prepared with your packets having already reviewed everything, that you have good preparation from an immigration expert. So we don't have to fall for lawyer fraud, we don't have to fall for notary fraud. Obviously we don't commit fraud either. It's important that from the beginning we protect ourselves from being another victim of immigration fraud. SEE YOU SOON

If they stay in the United States with their visa more than 1 year, then they have the 10 year bar. How do you acquire this bar? You only acquire the 3 or 10 year bar if you enter the United States either with a visa or illegally and leave. So the moment you leave to the outside, outside the United States, that's when you have a bar. I don't want you to get confused. ¿En qué consiste la ley? La ley “Show Me Your Papers” permite a las autoridades texanas solicitar la documentación migratoria a cualquier persona detenida o arrestada. creatives.transcript_en: Hello everyone. This is your immigration attorney Frances Arroyo speaking. I am a certified expert in immigration laws by the State Bar of California. I wanted to talk a little bit about the I-601A waiver process, which is the provisional waiver process that is done here inside the United States before obtaining your legal permanent residence at the consulate of your home country. This is a very delicate process and requires a lot of documentation. It is important in this process to do it in an individualized manner. How do we do it in our office, which is very different from other places? First of all, I do not give you a document list. Absolutely NOT. Many people who receive document lists from other immigration firms get confused. They don't know what applies to them. Here in this office, we conduct an individualized interview with you to see what documents you, specifically, need to achieve approval of your I-601A waiver. Remember that the legal standard for the 601A is to prove extreme hardship to a qualifying relative. So we have to interview you, get to know your life, get to know the lives of your qualifying relatives, whether it's a parent or spouse who is a resident or U.S. citizen, in order to achieve that approval in the most effective way. What we don't want is for you to submit a waiver that eventually gets a request for more evidence. We want to send it approvable from the beginning so that this provisional waiver flows through without any problems. Now, after they approve this provisional waiver, and the majority are approved in the office, we have the consular process left. We have had so much success in the office with our clients who have left with their waiver approved and return quickly back and arrived at our office with great joy, great excitement, because they have been able to obtain their legal permanent residence. We truly have the best team. From the moment my clients leave, we are monitoring step by step everything that happens during the interview and the process of their visa so they return to the United States with their family as they deserve. For me, I always tell all my clients the consular process, leaving the country, is the easiest step of the entire residence part. The family petition first and then the waiver, these are the really difficult parts. By the time you get to the consular process, leaving is such a calm, beautiful process, because here in the office we make sure you qualify and that you return perfectly well and safely to the United States. If you have any questions about this topic, we can help you here. Come see us.

creatives.transcript_en: The U visa is one of my favorite immigration benefits. Why? Because so many people qualify regardless of their immigration record. Let me explain the benefits of the U visa. If you qualify, you have to have been a victim of a violent crime. This is already established by law which crimes qualify, and you had to have cooperated with authorities. Once we have these requirements met, it's very important to have number one, the police report to determine eligibility. So this is always the first step to begin this U visa process. Number two, after that we have to ask the corresponding authorities for a certification which is a signature attesting that you have cooperated and that you were indeed a victim of this qualifying crime. Now, through the U visa, once we have the certification, we will file your application. The most beautiful thing at that moment is that we can get a work permit at the beginning of the process at immigration's discretion. We don't have to wait 5 or 6 years anymore to achieve this benefit. You can file it immediately with an application for a permit and they can grant it to you without having to wait as long as so many people have waited in the past. Now for the benefits, yes it's a five or six year wait, but now it's so beautiful to be able to wait with a work permit already. Additionally, when we're in this U visa process, it's so important to always do it with experts, people who know how to file this process. Imagine waiting 5 or 6 years and then having a denial. That's not worth it. We have to do it once and we have to do it correctly. I would hate to see that we would have to resubmit it and wait another six years. Why? Because of a simple error. So protect your application, protect yourself in this process. It's so important to file this with all the requirements. The most beautiful thing is that it doesn't matter if you entered illegally, if you've committed fraud, if you have certain crimes on your criminal record. These things are forgiven through the U visa process. The U visa is submitted with a waiver where we identify all the grounds of inadmissibility that can affect your application, and that way we ask for forgiveness at immigration's discretion. They grant it. So that's why this benefit qualifies so many people, because regardless of our criminal record or our immigration record, we can obviously submit this process. Remember, not everyone qualifies, so it's very important to review your case individually and assess your violations, your crimes, among other things that can affect your application. But after the approval of the U visa, you can submit for residency eventually after the years pass. This is so beautiful because it's one of the only humanitarian benefits that not only leads to residency but eventually to citizenship. There are so many elements of the U visa process and there's so much dynamic that has been changing over time, new benefits that have entered into this process. So if you have unfortunately been a victim of a crime, make sure you have the reports, make sure you come to the office to review it and begin your legalization process. We're waiting for you here!
