creatives.transcript_en: Hello everyone, I'm Abelsa French Arroyo, Immigration Attorney. I'm a certified expert in immigration law by the State Bar of California. Let's talk a little about immigration court, which is a huge topic. Let's focus on how we can win these cases. That's the most important thing. What we want when we start a deportation process is you've already entered the country, the judge, the government has given you a notice to appear in court. It's so important to speak with an immigration attorney first because not all cases are going to win. We know which cases are winners. In fact, the case law of the United States, the asylum laws already tell us which cases qualify and which don't. This is the good news right now. Even if we don't have a winning asylum case, we can obviously start that case if it's worthy to begin the work permit process, which is so important, our social security, but most importantly evaluate collateral benefits. What does this mean? Maybe we have a petition with the immigration judge but that doesn't mean it's our only option before the US government. Maybe yes with a judge but we have other options and other benefits. There are many people in court who can apply for immigration, for example, number one, juvenile visas for unaccompanied children or with one parent under 21 years old. Number two, U visa cases if you've been a victim of violent crime, cases under VAWA if you've been victims of domestic violence by a citizen spouse recently and minor child in the year. Also now we have TPS benefits for certain countries, meaning we can apply for TPS and be able to what? close the case in court. If we can start requesting prosecutorial discretion we can close or pause it in the courts to be able to work on other immigration benefits outside. This is what many people don't know entering the United States. There are other options that can be better than presenting your asylum case and we evaluate that, the experts, what are the possibilities or probabilities to win this case. Now if we're going to win the case we're going to present it 100%. We're with you until the end. But that decision is always made by the client with all the information about what collateral benefits are and what the probability is of winning the case. Remember that if a case is not won in Immigration Court, the alternative or one of the alternatives is deportation. Maybe it's voluntary departure if the judge grants it. But it's win or lose. The beautiful thing about these collateral benefits is that we don't have to take the case all the way to the end. And that's why it's so important to start your case with an immigration expert who can explain directly what these options are. And always work with an attorney in your court process, from beginning to end. Ask questions and show up to court. Make sure they're giving you updates on everything that happens step by step. Submit all necessary documents because if you don't submit them on time it can also result in a deportation order or can affect your case. Come see us if you're in process or if you already have a notice to go to court, we're waiting for you here.

creatives.transcript_en: Hello everyone, this is your immigration attorney Frances Arroyo. I am a certified expert in immigration law by the California State Bar. We have talked a lot about the Juvenile Visa that is granted to those children who have entered the United States without being accompanied by a parent or have entered the United States with one parent and the other parent has been a parent who has given the child negligence, abuse or abandonment. Now this is the circumstance that we have not talked about. I want to talk to the parents who have come with 1 child, 2 children but without the second mother or father here inside. What are your options within the Immigration Courts. If you have entered the United States with your child, single mother or father, and you are in front of an immigration judge, of course your children could possibly get the benefit of the juvenile visa. And when the juvenile visa process begins, the immigration judge by decree closes the children's case. Many parents ask me, And what about me? What happens to me when my child's case has been closed and I have to continue in front of the immigration judge facing a possible deportation order? The most important thing for parents to know is that there are options. The most important thing is to have an attorney who can explore those options. What we do in that circumstance can be many things. The first is to evaluate the asylum case, because if there is a case that we are going to win, we are going to present it well. Number two, use the tools of prosecutorial discretion to negotiate a way to be able to keep you here in the United States with your child. In my opinion it is in the child's interest to have their father, it is the most fundamental and the most fundamental right that exists in the world, that their parents or mothers be with the child. It is a basic human right, so we present asylum to the Courts to be able to keep this family united, this father, mother, son, daughter. There are other options as well. So when we are in this process, we believe that our children are going to be able to get the juvenile visa and eventually a residence. Don't think there are no options for you! There are options but the most important thing is that when you are in the immigration court process, you work with an expert in immigration law who can help you have a good future here with your children.

creatives.transcript_en: Hello everyone, this is your immigration attorney Frances Arroyo. I am a certified expert in Immigration Law by the California State Bar. Many clients come to my office to work on waivers for their cases. What are the steps to achieve an approvable waiver? Why do we have so much success here at Los Angeles Legal Advocates? I'm going to explain how we achieve waiver approvals in our office. First, there are different waivers with different requirements. The first thing you have to understand is how to classify the client, if they need some type of waiver. If it's a provisional waiver, if it's a criminal or fraud waiver or another, or if no waiver is needed at all. If we can proceed with your process without having to go through all this, the first step is making sure we know exactly what process we're in and what waiver we need to request with the application. It's so important to understand waiver requirements. For example, the most common waiver and the one we have maximum success with in the office is the provisional waiver, which is the waiver done inside the United States if in the future it will be a consular process. If you're going to leave the country to get your residency at a consulate or abroad. With this provisional waiver it's so important to know what the immigration adjudicator is looking for. Generally, what do these waivers have to include? And how do we win? First you have to have a qualifying relative, let's start with who qualifies. Many people and I've seen it have submitted their provisional waivers showing hardship to a child. As we know, children are not qualifying relatives for this type of waiver. It has to be a resident or citizen parent or a resident or citizen spouse. So we start with that, looking for extreme hardship to your qualifying relative. How do we do it? 1- We do an interview directly with the client and with the qualifying relative separately, why? Because all cases are completely different. We cannot give a generalized document list for each client. We don't do that in this office. We design an individualized list, depending on your interview with my team to understand in your case what those specific hardships are to be able to achieve success with your provisional waiver. And we have to show harm, emotional hardship, financial hardship possibly, if there's any type of medical hardship. And most important is where many people fail, many law firms fail, is showing the hardship for that qualifying relative in the event that you have to leave the country or that the qualifying relative has to relocate to another country. This hardship is very important to demonstrate and it has to be part of your waiver record. Many people fail here. If this isn't demonstrated, what can happen? Number one, there can be a denial of your waiver. And number two, the waiver can be delayed. It's possible that immigration will say show us what the relocation or separation hardships are. These two things are an important aspect. Understand that the adjudicator in their job with immigration when they're reading your waiver has a checklist they have to check off and we know exactly what's on that list of the people who make these decisions in your case. So your waiver cannot be sent if it's not complete with all these requirements. And because we always comply with these requirements and more, we achieve success in your waivers. So if you're going to start a process or if you're already in process and you don't know what's happening with your case, you haven't seen movement or communication, come see us. We're waiting for you here. We're ready to help you.

creatives.transcript_en: We have recently seen that the Immigration Department, USCIS is asking for more information and more evidence from people who are applying for an immigration benefit. They make this request through a letter called an RFE which means they are asking for more information or evidence to specifically indicate what is necessary for you. If you do not respond to this letter in the time they indicate in the letter, which can be 30 days. It can be 60 days or it can be up to 90 days. If you DO NOT RESPOND during this period of time your case can BE DENIED and it is very difficult to reopen the immigration case. So the moment YOU RECEIVE THIS LETTER you HAVE TO GO TO AN IMMIGRATION ATTORNEY because it may be that the thirty days count from the day you receive the letter.

creatives.transcript_en: First of all, if you receive a letter from the Immigration Department USCIS it can mean different things. The letter can be a receipt indicating that the process is pending, that immigration received your package and is processing it. You can also receive a letter indicating that you have to show up for a biometrics appointment where they will take your fingerprints and also a photo. You can also receive a letter from immigration indicating that you need to show up for an interview with an immigration officer, or it can be a letter asking for more evidence or a letter saying that a decision has been made on your case, it can be an approval or a denial of the case. So it all depends on the type of letter. But if you don't know what to do with this letter, right, if you don't know what it says or how this affects my process, it's very important to speak with an immigration attorney, take this letter and have the attorney explain to you what it says and what you have to do.

creatives.transcript_en: When your immigration case is referred to Immigration Court, you might be wondering what can I do now? Can I proceed with my case that I had with the Immigration Department? First of all, if you are already in Immigration Court, the most important thing is to speak with an immigration attorney. We already know that notaries, paralegals, people who prepare documents cannot appear before an immigration judge, nor can they appear before an immigration officer, but it is very important to trust your court case with a person who is an immigration attorney. Point number two: through Immigration Court, other doors open to receive immigration benefits. For example, what is called cancellation of removal. Cancellation of removal is an immigration process that gives an opportunity to immigrants who have been here more than 10 years physically in the United States and can demonstrate that, through their children, spouse, or parents, they will suffer in an extreme or uncommon way, that if let's say the father or mother is sent to their country, the children or spouse will suffer in an extreme way that is not common. So it is very important to determine if this can be an option for you. That they have placed you in court proceedings does not mean that your case no longer has options. It is very important to speak with an immigration attorney to see your options, if you can proceed with options before the immigration judge. Call us today to speak with our team of expert attorneys, call us, call our office to speak with our team of attorneys about your immigration case and see how we can help you in Immigration Court. You should always remember that being in Immigration Court you still have rights, and we are here to fight and defend your rights before the immigration judges.

creatives.transcript_en: Hi everyone, I'm attorney Laura León Eliado and I want to give you information about what the client told me about their appointment in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico. My client went to Ciudad Juárez, Mexico a week ago for their permanent residency interview and fortunately everything went well, their case was approved and they're already back in the United States as a permanent resident. creatives.transcript_en: If ICE detains you, is it worth fighting a case in Immigration Court? And the answer is yes. As an immigrant, no matter how you entered here in the United States, you have the right to fight your case in Court. The first thing you should know are your rights. First, you have the right to remain silent. You have the right to speak with an Immigration Judge and present your case or also receive legal advice from an immigration attorney. Second, you have the right to fight your case in different ways in Immigration Court. For example, if you're afraid to return to your country, you can apply for political asylum. If you have a family member like a spouse, children, or parents who are residents or American citizens, there's a possibility to fight what's called cancellation of removal.
